current_law.summary: Municipalities other than counties may adopt an impact fee ordinance, but only for off-site road (transportation) improvements listed in a transportation capital improvements plan, charged as a condition of final plat approval. The code authorizes no other kind of impact fee.

Before adopting a transportation impact fee, a municipality must appoint an advisory committee and prepare a transportation capital improvements plan built on land use assumptions and a roadway sufficiency analysis.
Sewer and water tap-in or connection fees must be worked out as the Municipality Authorities Act provides.
Subdivision and land development review fees must be reasonable and necessary and set by a fee schedule adopted by ordinance or resolution.
